subject.title: Feature: Distinguish webchat client types (Mac app vs browser)

question: Should agent-visible WebChat client type be exposed as gateway-attested connect metadata, as an explicitly untrusted client hint, or not exposed to agents?
rationale: Agents could use this field for native-only behavior, deep links, diagnostics, or privileged UX, so automation should not decide the trust semantics or carrier shape without maintainer security/product intent.

options.title: Gateway-attested metadata
options.body: Propagate the validated `connect.client` identity into a narrow runtime metadata field and document exactly what agents may trust.

options.title: Untrusted diagnostic hint
options.body: Expose only a clearly labeled untrusted hint for debugging and forbid agents from treating it as a capability or permission signal.

options.title: Decline runtime exposure
options.body: Keep client identity limited to Gateway connection diagnostics until a stronger client-attestation design exists.

recommendation.title: Gateway-attested metadata
recommendation.body: Propagate the validated `connect.client` identity into a narrow runtime metadata field and document exactly what agents may trust.

likelyOwner.reason: The current client identity registry and protocol extraction history point to the Gateway protocol boundary as the decision center.
